Jia: Quick heads-up — noticed a throughput drop on Dedicated during a spike of small-seq requests (~seq_len 16-48). Profiling suggests we fell back from FlashAttention -> hybrid kernel more often and paged-KV page faults increased. Anyone else seeing this?
Devon: saw same in us-west-2 p3 pool at ~12:10 UTC, spike correlates with chatty customers. rough numbers: throughput -18% tail latency +45%.
Sam: can you paste the perf snapshot? did kernel selector fallback due to OOM or seq pattern?
perf-bot: Profiling snapshot (1799001234):
- Kernel switches: Flash->Hybrid xfer 4.2k requests (11% of total)
- Avg queue wait (small-seq): 14.8ms -> 38.2ms during spike
- PagedKV page faults increased 3.6x
- Token-level cost +9%
Devon: here's raw log snippet:
```
[12:10:14] batcher: formed batch size=6 seq=32 avg_wait=39ms selected_kernel=hybrid
[12:10:14] runtime: flash_kernel_fallback(reason=insufficient_workspace)
[12:10:14] pagedkv: page_miss=1 alloc_retry=1
```
Maria: hypothesis: continuous batcher token_budget_target too aggressive for small-seq -> batches small but frequent causing kernel to choose hybrid because workspace fragmentation. propose increasing token_budget_target for small_seq class from 512->1024 and raise max_queue_time_ms from 30->50.
Avery: also think kernel selector threshold for flash requires contiguous workspace; pagedKV adds indirection, so combined effect causes fallback. We should prefer flash if batch_size>=8 or seq>=64; otherwise use hybrid. Add hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping.
Sam: can we try a canary with these changes? PR to change heuristics + metric to track kernel_flip_rate and avg_workspace_free_bytes.
Jia: I'll spin up a canary branch: changes:
```
continuous_batcher:
  small_seq_token_budget_target: 1024
  max_queue_time_ms: 50
kernel_selector:
  prefer_flash_if: "batch_size>=8 or seq_len>=64"
  hysteresis_ms: 200
pagedkv:
  prefetch_window: 2
```
Devon: I'll run the canary on us-west-2 dedicated pool and collect kernel_switch_count, avg_wait_by_seq, pagedkv_page_fault_rate.
perf-bot: Canary started at 12:45 UTC. Baseline -> canary comparison will be posted.
Maria: if canary looks good, follow-up: add profiler tag to trace per-request kernel decisions so we can correlate prompts to flips.
Sam: ack. assign owners: Jia -> deploy canary, Devon -> metrics + dashboards, Maria -> follow-up tracing. ETA EOD.
Devon: sounds good. starting runs now :rocket:
Jia: thanks — will post results in this thread.
